name: What to Do When Your Allen Roof Shows Storm Damage

step.name: Step 1: Ensure safety and prevent further damage. After the storm, check your property from a safe distance for downed power lines, gas leaks, or structural hazards before getting too close. If there are active leaks, place buckets to catch water and cover damaged areas with tarps if it's safe to do so. Your immediate priority is to stop further water intrusion to protect your home's interior.

step.name: Step 2: Document all damage with photos and videos. Before any cleanup or repairs begin, grab your phone or camera and thoroughly photograph and video all visible damage, both exterior and interior. Capture wide shots to show context and close-ups of specific issues like missing shingles, dented gutters, or water stains on ceilings. Make sure to note the date and time you took these pictures.

step.name: Step 3: Contact your insurance company promptly. Don't delay reporting potential storm damage. Review your policy for specific claim deadlines, but generally, the sooner you notify them, the better. They’ll open a claim and explain their process for assessment. Be prepared to share your documentation of the damage you've collected.

We'll identify all affected areas, distinguish storm damage from normal wear, and provide the clear documentation you'll need for your insurance claim. We'll also help you understand if the damage is substantial enough to warrant a claim or if minor repairs are more cost-effective.

step.name: Step 5: Preserve receipts for emergency repairs. If you had to make any emergency repairs, like tarping your roof to prevent more leaks, keep all receipts. Your insurance company may reimburse you for these reasonable costs, so careful record-keeping is important. Avoid discarding any damaged materials until your insurer or a professional evaluator has had a chance to inspect them.

step.name: Step 6: Review all estimates and insurance adjustor reports. Once your professional assessment is complete and your insurance adjustor has visited, compare the findings. Ensure that both reports align and that all damage is accounted for. If there are discrepancies, ask for clarification. Don't sign anything you don't fully understand.
step.text: Dealing with storm damage on your Allen roof can feel overwhelming, but taking these steps will help you manage the situation effectively. For expert help with your roof damage assessment, reach out to Discounted Roofing Co. for a free estimate!
